items.raw_snippet: Fran Fernandez meets up with Derek Crager, founder of Practical AI and author of Human First AI, to explore a different way of thinking about artificial intelligence: not as a replacement for people, but as a way to amplify what they can do. Drawing on his experience building employee training at Amazon, Derek explains how AI can put expertise in the hands of frontline workers, close knowledge gaps in real time, and help organizations create measurable value without vacating human judgment. [...] AI can turn scarce expertise into an always-available resource. Organizations rarely have enough subject matter experts to support every employee at the moment a problem occurs. AI can draw from manuals, SOPs, processes, and organizational knowledge to act as a scalable mentor or sounding board, helping employees troubleshoot problems without waiting for an expert to become available. [...] The best opportunities often sit inside mundane work and knowledge gaps. Repetitive tasks and delays caused by missing information consume time without taking advantage of human creativity. AI and automation can reduce that burden, while people focus on troubleshooting, continuous improvement, creative problem-solving, and decisions that fall outside automation's predefined boundaries.

The easiest trap in AI is leading with “what can it do?” That’s what headlines and product announcements talk about. I coach customers to ask a different question: what _should_ it do here?
